  PROBLEM: Defensive-coding inconsistency. The `git add` command uses `"${AGENTS_FILE}"` without the `:-` default, whereas surrounding control flow and other uses of variables in this script employ the `${VAR:-}` pattern.
  WHY: With `set -u` enabled, if `AGENTS_FILE` were ever unset or empty, `"${AGENTS_FILE}"` would resolve correctly as an empty string (as it is quoted), but if it were truly unset (not just empty), `set -u` might cause an abort depending on shell behavior for quoted unset variables, though `"${VAR:-}"` is the standard safe pattern here. Given the context (the `if` block above it checks if assembled is "true"), it is likely defined, making this a low-risk inconsistency.

  PROBLEM: The two sibling blocks inside the same `if [ "${AGENTS_ASSEMBLED:-}" = "true" ]; then` guard use different defensive patterns for the same shell variable. Line 899 uses `${AGENTS_FILE}` (which under `set -u` aborts on an unset value) while line 965 uses `${AGENTS_FILE:-}` (substitutes empty string).
  WHY: Today it does not — the `assemble_agents.py` `_write_outputs` call (`scripts/assemble_agents.py:432-437`) sets `agents_assembled`, `agents_file`, and `agents_fragment_count` together, so when `AGENTS_ASSEMBLED` is `"true"`, `AGENTS_FILE` is also set. However, the asymmetry is defensible to flag because: (1) `set -euo pipefail` is active on line 845, so any future bug in `assemble_agents.py` that emits `agents_assembled=true` without `agents_file` would crash on line 899 before reaching line 965 (which would silently produce "agents.d fragments assembled into  (0 fragment(s))."); (2) the new `test_consumer_sync_folds_agents_fragments_and_reports_them` assertion locks in the `${AGENTS_FILE}` form, propagating the inconsistency into the test contract. Aligning line 899 to `"${AGENTS_FILE:-}"` would close the divergence with a one-token edit. Note: this is purely a defensive-coding alignment, not a triggered bug.
